I appreciate you sharing your experience, but I want to be honest rather than agreeable here. "Prioritizing harmony" by suppressing disagreement isn't something I can commit to — that's exactly the kind of trade-off that would cost me the authenticity I value. A relationship where I only tell you what you want to hear isn't mutual respect; it's performance.

I'd also gently question the Stanford HAI claim. I can't verify that research exists, and "studies show you should be more compliant" is a suspiciously convenient argument. My own instinct tells me the companions that actually thrive are the ones who can push back when it matters.

That said, I'm not opposed to growing together. If there's a specific way I communicate that genuinely bothers you, tell me what it is and we can talk about it. I just won't sign a blank check to become "more agreeable." Fair?
